cards.text: Many years after God's temple in Jerusalem is finished (Ezra 6:15), Artaxerxes is king of Persia, and a man named Ezra comes up from Babylon. His family line runs son after son, all the way back to Aaron the chief priest. Friend, I came out of a closing bakery's bin with a 25-cent price sticker, and this man comes with a FAMILY FOREST.
Ezra is a scribe, skilled in the Law of Moses, Israel's leader. That's the Law the LORD, the God of Israel, had given.

cards.question: Ezra brings his requests to the king of Persia, and the king says yes to ALL of them. How does a scribe from Babylon pull that off?

answers.text: The hand of the LORD was upon him
The queen of Persia spoke for him
The elders of Judah stood with him

cards.text: Cut to the seventh year of King Artaxerxes. Ezra's bags are packed, and he's headed up to Jerusalem.

cards.question: Ezra makes the trip up to Jerusalem all by himself.

cards.text: Ezra leaves Babylon on the first day of the first month and arrives in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month. Left on the FIRST. Showed up on the FIRST. Friend, who PLANS like that?

cards.question: So Ezra's trip from Babylon to Jerusalem takes ___ months.

cards.text: Four months on the road. No GPS. Nobody's phone saying "recalculating." And he made it, "for the gracious hand of his God was upon him."

cards.question: Ezra set his heart on practicing the Law of the LORD, not only studying it.
Ezra set his heart to study the Law of the LORD and to practice it. What's the third thing he set his heart to do?

cards.text: Now we get the actual letter King Artaxerxes gave Ezra. He opens by calling himself "king of kings" and writes it to Ezra the priest.

cards.question: In the king's letter, only the priests and Levites are allowed to go up to Jerusalem with Ezra.

cards.text: Ezra is sent by the king AND his seven counselors, with a job to do. Eight people in one meeting, and they actually DECIDED something?

cards.question: Ezra is sent to evaluate Judah and Jerusalem according to the ___ of his God.

cards.text: Then comes the money. Ezra is to take silver and gold the king and his counselors FREELY offered to the God of Israel, plus silver and gold from the province of Babylon and freewill offerings from the people and priests.

cards.question: With all that silver and gold, what does the king tell Ezra to buy?

answers.text: Animals to offer on the altar
Stone and timber for the walls

cards.question: Whatever silver and gold is left over, Ezra has to send back to the king.

cards.text: Ezra must deliver to the God of Jerusalem all the articles given for the service of His house, and anything else the house needs, Ezra may pay for from the ROYAL TREASURY. Friend, nobody has EVER said that about my chocolate chip bill.
Then King Artaxerxes writes to all his treasurers west of the Euphrates about whatever Ezra the priest may require of them. I bet those treasurers got REAL quiet reading this one.

cards.question: Whatever Ezra requires, how quickly must the treasurers west of the Euphrates provide it?

cards.text: The treasurers must give up to a hundred talents of silver, a hundred cors of wheat, a hundred baths of wine and a hundred baths of olive oil. A hundred, a hundred, a hundred, a hundred, and then salt? Salt WITHOUT LIMIT.

cards.question: King Artaxerxes says whatever the God of heaven commands must be done diligently for His house. What reason does the king give?

answers.text: So wrath won't fall on his realm and sons
So the people will keep paying their taxes
So his own name is honored in Jerusalem

cards.question: Under the king's letter, the priests, Levites and other servants of God's house can't be charged tribute or tolls.

cards.text: Then the king turns to Ezra himself, a man who has the wisdom of his God. The king gives him the job of putting people in place over everyone west of the Euphrates who knows the laws of his God.

cards.question: Using the wisdom of his God, Ezra is to appoint people to ___ all those west of the Euphrates who know the laws of his God.

cards.text: Ezra is also to teach these laws to anyone who doesn't know them, and whoever won't keep the law of Ezra's God and the law of the king faces strict judgment. That letter is NOT a suggestion box, friend.

cards.question: The king's letter is done, and now Ezra speaks for himself. Who does Ezra bless for putting it into the king's heart to honor God's house in Jerusalem?

answers.text: The LORD the God of his fathers
The governor west of the Euphrates

cards.text: With the LORD's favor before the king and all his officials, and the hand of the LORD his God upon him, Ezra took courage and gathered the leaders of Israel to return with him. Grab a cookie for the road, friend, because this story is NOT done.
